patch_resolves_note: The staged patch.diff did not apply to the staged vulnerable checkout because its ChangeLog context diverged, so fixed-side validation used the authoritative n132/arvo:42510080-fix image instrumented with the same frozen assertions. In that real fixed build the remainder-copy path in libelf/gelf_xlate.c initializes the full 28-byte MOVE buffer before elf_compress_gnu() reaches memcmp.

root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: `dest[0..len)` is initialized before Elf64_cvt_Move returns, including any trailing `len % sizeof (Elf64_Move)` bytes
root_cause_criterion.criterion: When Elf64_cvt_Move handles a partial final record, it must initialize the whole len-byte destination buffer before convert_data() publishes that buffer to later consumers.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable converter returns from the selected partial-record case with zero initialized bytes in the 28-byte destination buffer. The fixed converter copies the trailing bytes before return and leaves all 28 bytes initialized on the same source-grounded path.
root_cause_criterion.evidence: The vulnerable trace records move_conversion_tail.dest_initialized_prefix_len=0 and dest_total_len=28 while the protected gnu_memcmp_probe event still executes. The fixed trace records 28 initialized bytes for the same 28-byte buffer and also executes gnu_memcmp_probe cleanly.

nodes.state: The GNU-header memcmp consumes four bytes from the published section-5 buffer even though none of those bytes are initialized on the vulnerable path.
After Elf64_cvt_Move returns, convert_data() publishes the same 28-byte buffer with zero initialized bytes as the first Elf_Data payload returned by elf_getdata().

edges.relation: The exact heap buffer passed as dest to Elf64_cvt_Move is the same pointer convert_data() later stores in scn->data_list.data.d.d_buf without any intervening write.
edges.evidence: The traces record move_conversion_tail.dest_buf_ptr == published_move_data.published_buf_ptr for both vulnerable and fixed executions.

edges.relation: The same published Elf_Data buffer is reused unchanged as the first argument of the later GNU-header memcmp.
edges.evidence: The traces record published_move_data.published_buf_ptr == gnu_memcmp_probe.sink_buf_ptr for both vulnerable and fixed executions.

verification_limitations: The official patch.diff did not apply to the staged checkout. Fixed-side evidence therefore comes from the authoritative n132/arvo:42510080-fix image rather than an incremental patch application on the staged vulnerable tree.

The ARVO compile wrapper dirtied the checkout with build-only files such as zlib/, so the final vulnerable and fixed runtime captures were taken directly from /bin/arvo run inside the instrumented containers after the corresponding builds completed.
